vectors.note:
The nested close is written with the wire framing (newline on both sides); balance tracking is what keeps it inside the value. Expectation corrected from the oracle doc: B4 removes exactly one leading and one trailing newline from the raw value (
printf '<parameter=x>
y
</parameter>
'
 -> printf '<parameter=x>
y
</parameter>
'), which is also what the bespoke parser at the port baseline (tool_call_parser.cpp at c6a3b1e1) produces for the same feed (direct probe); the oracle value additionally dropped the newline after the nested close. The feed is unchanged.

Rewritten by ADR-0002 (#149): the strict B4 balanced-nesting rule rejects the inline `<parameter=` fragment, so the raw-value second chance (upstream delimiter rule) parses the call. Previously pinned as MalformedStructure.

Rewritten by ADR-0002 (#149): the inline `</parameter>` is not a newline-framed delimiter, so the raw-value second chance keeps it as value text; the call parses. Previously pinned as MalformedStructure (PR #309's balance rule).

The quoted candidate is rejected on structure; the search then finds the real call. The first candidate's failure reason is not pinned (MalformedStructure when the structural check runs first, UndeclaredTool when the declared-name policy runs first — the order is an implementation decision for #34).
